CONFIDENTIAL

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
Sec. 1. Special Branch Station 40
REPORT
Date July 16, 19 40.

Subject Japanese Military to convene meetings of owners of industrial
concerns now controlled by them on July 24 and 30.

Made by D.I. Kao Yen Ken Forwarded by D.I. Crawford

The "Committee for the Readjustment of Factories
under the Control of the Army in Shanghai Area" (previou-
ly known as the "Factory Returning Committee") of the
Japanese Military Headquarters at Soochow is arranging
to convene a meeting of the owners of local Chinese
cotton mills now under the control of the Japanese Army
for 3 p.m. July 24 in the Astor House on Whangpoo Road.
A similar meeting of owners of industrial concerns other
than cotton mills has also been convened for 3 p.m. July
30 at the same venue.

According to the executives of the "Shanghai
Office of the Committee for Taking Over of Factories now
Under Japanese Military Occupation of the Ministry of
Industries and Commerce of the New Central Government",
449 Haining Road, the Japanese Military Authorities during
these meetings will explain to the Chinese owners their
intention to return the concerns to the rightful owners
and will instruct them to complete their applications
through the "Shanghai Office of the Ministry of Industries
and Commerce" at 449 Haining Road, should they desire the
return of their property.

It is stated that Major General Sakurai (櫻井少将)
is in charge of the "Committee for the Readjustment of
Factories" of the Japanese Military.

报告
日期：1940年7月16日。

事由：日军拟于7月24日和30日召集目前由其控制的工业企业业主开会。

由督察员高恩肯（Kao Yen Ken）呈报，经督察员克劳福德（Crawford）转呈

驻苏州的日本军事总部下属的“上海地区陆军管理工厂调整委员会”（前称“工厂发还委员会”）正安排于7月24日下午3时，在黄浦路礼查饭店（Astor House）召开目前处于日军控制下的当地中国棉纺厂业主会议。另一次类似的非棉纺厂工业企业业主会议也已定于7月30日下午3时在同一地点召开。

据位于海宁路449号的“新中央政府工商部接收日军管理工厂委员会驻沪办事处”主管人员称，在上述会议期间，日本军方当局将向中国业主说明其将企业归还原主的意图，并指示那些希望收回财产的业主通过海宁路449号的“工商部驻沪办事处”完成申请手续。

据悉，樱井少将（Major General Sakurai）负责日本军方的“工厂调整委员会”。

归档
高恩肯（Kao Yen Ken）
督察员

副 commissioner（特别科）。

1940年6月1日，“新中央政府工商部接收日军管理工厂委员会驻沪办事处”（工商部接收日軍管理工廠委員會駐沪辦事處）由工商部理事兼驻沪办事处主任金祖惠（CHING TSO WEI）先生在北四川路附近的海宁路449号成立。该办事处于1940年6月12日开始运作，职员包括3名文员。

该办事处规定，所有位于目前日军占领领土内的工厂业主或管理层，应在三个月内向驻沪办事处提交申请。收到申请后，驻沪办事处将对申请表中所含细节展开调查，随后将申请报送工商部审批。当申请获得南京当局批准并退回驻沪办事处后，驻沪办事处将联系当地日军总部以办理财产归还事宜。

驻沪办事处不向申请人收取任何费用，所有申请均作为严格机密事项处理。

APPENDIX "A"

Rules for Submitting application for the Return
of Factories under Military Occupation.
............
1.Owners of factories which are located in Japanese
Military occupied areas may apply for the return
of their property in accordance with the provisions
set out in these rules.
2.Owners of factories which are under military occupation
must fulfil the following provisions :-
(a) Sole proprietor or his legal representative or
agent.
(b) Legal representative of a company.
(c) Persons having legal claims on such factories
may report such rights to the Government in
accordance with the provisions laid down in
these rules.
3.Owners of factories under military occupation should
fill in an application form applying for the return
of factories under military occupation together with
all necessary documents and plans for resumption of
operations and forward same to the competent authorities
for endorsement.
4.Owners of factories under military occupation should
apply for the return of their factories within a
period of three months after promulgation of these
rules.
5.Should the owners of factories under military occupation
fail to apply for the return of their property after
the stipulated period or should their application be
refused for any reason, such factories will revert
to the Government.
pages.zh:
附录 “A”

申请归还军事占领下工厂的规则。
............
1. 位于日军占领区的工厂业主，可根据本规则规定的条款申请归还其财产。
2. 处于军事占领下的工厂业主必须履行以下规定：-
(a) 独资经营者或其合法代表人或代理人。
(b) 公司的合法代表人。
(c) 对此类工厂拥有合法权利的人，可根据本规则规定的条款向政府申报此类权利。
3. 处于军事占领下的工厂业主应填写申请归还军事占领下工厂的申请表，连同所有必要文件及恢复运营计划，一并送交主管当局签注。
4. 处于军事占领下的工厂业主应在本规则颁布后的三个月内申请归还其工厂。
5. 若处于军事占领下的工厂业主在规定期限后未申请归还其财产，或其申请因任何原因被拒绝，此类工厂将收归政府所有。

6. Factories should resume work within one month after
the date of taking over from the military authorities,
failing which, such factories will be taken over
and managed by the Government.
7. After taking over from the military authorities,
factories should be operated in principle by the
bona fide owners themselves, but if connected with
Japanese commercial interests, the factories should
be operated in accordance with the principle of
equality and reciprocity.
8. Any contract of co-operation entered into by the
owners of factories and Japanese interests both prior
to and after taking over from the Japanese military
authorities should be submitted for approval to the
Government.
9. Owners of factories under military occupation having
entered into contracts with Japanese commercial interests
prior to the promulgation of these rules, may apply
for a readjustment of such contracts when conditions
are prejudicial to the interests of the owners.
10. Permission of the Government should be obtained for
the use of foreign capital for the operation of
factories formerly under military occupation.
11. All expenses incurred by the military authorities in
the maintenance of such factories prior to the taking
over should be defrayed by the owners concerned.
12. These rules will be in force after the date of pro-
mulgation.

DATE 13 / 7 / 40

On June 1, 1940, the "Shanghai Office of the Committee for Taking Over of Factories Now under Japanese Military Occupation of Ministry of Industries and Commerce of the New Central Government" (工商部接管日軍管理工廠委員會駐沪辦事處) was established at 449, Haining Road near North Szechuen Road, by Mr. CHING TSO WEI (金祖惠), a Councillor of the Ministry of Industry and Commerce and concurrently Chief of the Shanghai Office. This office commenced functioning on June 12, 1940 with a staff of 3 clerks.

The regulations of the office provide that owners or the management of all factories situated in territory at present under Japanese military occupation should file applications within a period of three months with the Shanghai Office. On receipt of an application, the Shanghai Office will commence an investigation into the details contained in the application form, following which, the application will be forwarded to the Ministry of Industries and Commerce for approval. When the application is approved and returned to the Shanghai Office by the Nanking authorities the local headquarters of the Japanese Army will be approached by the Shanghai Office for the return of the property.

No charge will be levied by the Shanghai Office on applicants and all applications will be treated as a strictly confidential matter.

S. g.

Subject Operation of Chinese Factory by Japanese.

Made by D.S.I. McCahey, Forwarded by [签名]

Sir,

On May 16th it was ascertained that the Kung Chin
Iron Works (公勤铁厂), 66 Linching Road, a Chinese
concern, was being operated by Japanese. On May 17th
J.D.S. Osano was instructed to make enquiries which
resulted in the fact that the Japanese management of
the Asia Steel and Iron Works, 379 Hochien Road are
operating the Kung Chin Iron Works and employing between
fifteen and twenty Chinese labourers (this number will
probably be increased) to manufacture wire nails etc for
Japanese Military purposes.

Mr. K.F. Hwan, General Manager, was communicated with
by telephone with a view to ascertaining whether he had
been approached by aforesaid Japanese concern. He
denied having been approached but stated he was aware of
the factory being operated and that he had instructed his
lawyer to investigate.

Questioned as to whether any of the property stored
in the factory belonged to subjects of a third power
Mr. Hwan replied all third party property had been removed
and that wire and nails stored in a godown on the premises
belonged to his company.

Endeavours will be made to ascertain whether this
godown has been forced by the present operators.

Your obedient servant,

[签名]

先生，

5月16日查明，位于临青路66号的中资企业公勤铁厂（Kung Chin Iron Works）正由日本人经营。5月17日，指令日籍警探小佐野（J.D.S. Osano）进行调查，结果证实，河间路379号亚细亚钢铁厂（Asia Steel and Iron Works）的日方管理层正在经营公勤铁厂，并雇佣了十五至二十名中国劳工（此人数可能会增加），为日本军方制造铁丝钉等物品。

已通过电话与总经理黄克夫（Mr. K.F. Hwan）先生联系，以确认他是否曾被上述日本公司接洽。他否认曾被接洽，但表示知晓该工厂正在运营，且已指示其律师进行调查。

当被问及储存在工厂内的任何财产是否属于第三国国民时，黄先生回答说所有第三方财产已被移除，存放在厂区仓库内的铁丝和钉子属于其公司所有。

我们将努力查明该仓库是否被当前经营者强行占用。

您忠实的仆人，

Subject Japanese taking over the Heng Foong Cotton Mill 1-6 Wahshing Road.

Made by D.I.Hutton Forwarded by ...

Sir:

With reference to a telephone message from Mr. Young Acting Commissioner of Police I beg to report that the present situation at the Heng Foong Cotton Mill 1-6 Wahshing Road was ascertained by J.S.S. 149.

For several months the owners of the Dah Kong Cotton Mill (Japanese) have been in charge of the Heng Foong Mill and have had Chinese employees on the premises repairing machinery under the supervision of Japanese. Japanese troops were in occupation of the mill in June but for some time now they have not occupied the premises.

From information received by J.S.S. 149 the Dah Kong Company intend opening the mill at an early date.

The former owners of the Heng Foong Mill refused to co-operate with the Japanese and as far as can be ascertained the Dah Kong Mill obtained their rights to operate the mill from the Japanese Special Naval Service Mission.

As will be seen from previous reports re the Heng Foong Mill this property was taken over by the Industrial Development Company (British) and registered at the H.B.M.Consulate on 15/11/37.

D.I.

制作人：D.I.Hutton 转呈人：...

先生：

参照代理警务处长 Young 先生的电话留言，谨报告如下：第149号日本特别分部（J.S.S. 149）查明了位于华兴路（Wahshing Road）1-6号的恒丰纱厂目前的状况。

数月来，大康纱厂（日本）的业主一直负责管理恒丰纱厂，并雇佣中国雇员在日军监督下修理机器。日军曾于六月占领该厂，但目前已有一段时间未占据该处所。

根据第149号日本特别分部（J.S.S. 149）收到的情报，大康公司打算近期开设该厂。

恒丰纱厂的前业主拒绝与日本人合作，据查，大康纱厂是从日本海军特别任务团（Japanese Special Naval Service Mission）获得经营该厂的权利。

从此前关于恒丰纱厂的报告中可以看出，该产业已被（英国）工业发展公司接管，并于1937年11月15日在英国驻华领事馆注册。

Made by D. C. White Forwarded by [Signature]
Sir:
On the 19/5/38 I applied for information at Siemens Co. Ltd.,
Nanking Road, regarding the last owner of the dynamos mentioned
in the report of D.C. Lockwood (p. 4), when it was learnt that the
dynamos in question had been sold about 8 years ago, the buyer(s)
however are not known, Siemens nevertheless will endeavour to
trace the little property if expected. On the order of the
29/5/38, D.C. Lockwood, Indian Detectives and the undersigned
kept observation on the American Auctioneering Co., 625 Szechuen
Road but none of the suspected Indians arrived. These four dynamos
will be taken to Central Station on the 21/5/38 and the staff of
the American Auctioneering Co. will be requested to detain any
person attempting to claim the dynamos and notify Central Station.
During the afternoon of the 20/5/38, the undersigned and
S.D.C. 102 questioned Lochran Singh, (S.P. No. 303) at Yulin Road
Station but in spite of carefully questioning, denied knowledge
of the dynamos adding that the witnesses had probably mistaken
him for some other Indian as to most Chinese one Indian is more
or less like another. As nothing concrete could be attached to
this man, he was therefore released.
It should be mentioned that the dynamos in question are not
part of those which have been stolen from the Heng Foon Mill.
Inquiries proceeding.
[Signature]
Senior Detective in Charge.

先生：
1938年5月19日，我就 D.C. Lockwood 报告（第4页）中提到的发电机的最后所有者一事，向南京路的西门子有限公司（Siemens Co. Ltd.）查询信息，得知所述发电机大约在8年前售出，但买家不详，尽管如此，西门子公司将尽力追踪这批小额财产若被期待的话。根据5月29日的命令，D.C. Lockwood、印度侦探及本人在四川路625号的美国拍卖行（American Auctioneering Co.）进行监视，但嫌疑印度人均未出现。这四台发电机将于1938年5月21日送往中央捕房，并将要求美国拍卖行的员工扣留任何试图认领发电机的人，并通知中央捕房。

Date May 18, 1938.
Subject Disposal of suspected stolen property by British Indians =
Sale of dynamos by American Auctioneering Co., 625 Szechuen Road.
Made by and Forwarded by D.S. Lockwood.

Following the report of a theft of a number of dynamos from the Heng Foon Cotton Mill, Nos. 1 - 6 Whashing Road, the staff of S.4 Special Branch were instructed to ascertain whether Indians were responsible for the removal of the dynamos and, if attempts had been made to dispose of them in the area south of the creek. During the morning of May 18, 1938, information was received that four Indians, during the past month, had disposed of a number of electrical machines, and that on May 14, 1938, the American Auctioneering Co., 625 Szechuen Road, had been instructed to sell by auction four dynamos bearing the following serial numbers:- 2755788, 2755705, 3545637, 3642503, manufactured by Siemens Co., Ltd., Germany.

Enquiries show that the four Indians concerned in the disposal of the machines are:-

Bur Singh s/o Vir Singh
Village and Post Office Lauhka
District Amritsar.

Lachhman Singh s/o Jawala Singh P.W. No. 303
Village Dhariwal Post Office Dhilwan
District Jullundur.

Hari Singh s/o Lachhman Singh
Village and Post Office Sursingh
District Lahore.

Dewa Singh s/o Santa Singh

Sir:
Re D.C.Crime's remarks, "P.A.Sinza case arrests?" inquiries made at Pina Station revealed that the men in custody had no connection with this case. Re A.C.Siths remarks, "No S.R.W. 454 on our books;" the watchman in question is No. 260 employed at 51 Yangchow Road, this mistake being a typographical error.
Further inquiries made in connection with this case have proven abortive. The assistance of the Indian Section is being sought to have inquiries made among the Indian Watchmen.
At 6.50 pm 11/5/38, Indian Watchman named Kehar Singh employed at the Heng Foong Cotton & Spinning Mill No. 1-6 Wharsing Road reported that at about 5.30 pm 11/5/38 four Japanese civilians had removed four dynamos from the mill premises and transported same away on a motor truck bearing S.M.C. Lic. No. 20210.
Enquiries at the Traffic Office revealed that the vehicle used was owned by the Dah Kong Cotton & Spinning Co. No. 195 Tengyueh Road (Japanese), therefore J.D.S.149 proceeded to that address and ascertained that the Dah Kong Mill have been appointed by the Japanese Special Military Mission Astor House to prepare the Heng Foong Mill machinery etc. ready for use, since they anticipate resuming operations there in the near future.
The Dah Kong representative admitted having removed the four dynamos stating that they had done so to effect repairs to them, after which they would be returned. He also added that in the near future more machinery would be removed from the mill & taken away to be repaired.
The four dynamos are at present being kept at the Dah Kong Mill.
The owner will be informed am 12/5/38.
D.S.24.

经向交通处查询，所用车辆属于大康棉纺公司（Dah Kong Cotton & Spinning Co.），地址：腾越路195号（日本），因此第149号日本特别分部（J.D.S.149）前往该地址，查明大康纱厂已受日本驻沪海军特别任务团（Astor House）委派，准备恒丰纱厂的机器等以备使用，因为他们预计不久将在该处恢复运营。

Subject Theft of electric dynamos from the Heng Foong Cotton Mill
No.1-6 Hashing Road.

Made by I.C. 24 White. Forwarded by

Sir,
On the 19/4/38 information was received from the Shanghai Brokerage Co., 405 Hongkong & Shanghai Bank Building, agents for the Italian owners of the Heng Foong Cotton Mill, No.1-6 Hashing Rd to the effect that a number of electric dynamos had been stolen from the spinning dept: of the mill. From subsequent inquiries made by J.D.S.149 and the undersigned ascertained the following:-. On the 13-16/4/38 a number of Chinese prisoners of war escorted by Japanese troops were working in the mill cleaning away the debris left behind by the last contingent of Japanese troops who had occupied the mill. From the 14/4/38 to 18/4/38 the mill was left open protected at day by two Indian and one Italian private watchmen, and one Indian private watchman by night, all employees of the Shanghai Brokerage Co.; there is also one Indian private watchman on night duty in the employ of the Dah Kong Cotton Mill, Y'poo Rd. From the 14th-18/4/38 a Mr.S.Hugimaru, employee of the Dah Kong Mill, visited the Heng Foong Mill daily and found everything correct. On the 18/4/38 when he again visited the mill he discovered twenty-four dynamos missing.

The watchmen employed on day duty by the Shanghai Brokerage Co. when questioned stated that they had inspected the mill on the 17/4/38 and found everything in order, but on the 18/4/38 they discovered that the dynamos had been removed. The watchman Fouja Singh employed on night duty by the Shanghai Brokerage Co. stated that he neither heard nor saw anyone in or near the mill on the night of 17/4/38; this, however is only to be expected as this watchman is also employed at 260 Yangchow Rd as S.P.W.454 during day time, it is therefore safe to presume that when on duty at the mill he sleeps throughout the night, this he denies.

（印：25 APR. 1938 SPECIAL BRANCH）
（批注：S.C. / S.4 / 38P / 25/4）

制作人：I.C. 24 White。 转呈人：

先生，
1938年4月19日，收到来自上海经纪行（Shanghai Brokerage Co.，地址：汇丰银行大楼405室，恒丰纱厂意大利业主的代理人）的消息，称该厂纺纱部有多台电动发电机被盗。经第149号日本特别分部（J.D.S.149）及本人随后的查询，查明如下情况：1938年4月13日至16日，一批由中国战俘组成的队伍在日军护送下在厂内工作，清理上一批占领该厂的日军留下的废墟。1938年4月14日至18日，该厂白天由两名印度人和一名意大利私人看守保护，夜间由一名印度私人看守保护，均为上海经纪行的雇员；此外，还有一名受雇于耶普路（Y'poo Rd.）大康纱厂的印度私人看守值夜班。1938年4月14日至18日，大康纱厂雇员 S.Hugimaru 先生每天访问恒丰纱厂，发现一切正常。1938年4月18日，当他再次访问该厂时，发现二十四台发电机失踪。

上海经纪行雇用的日间看守在接受询问时表示，他们于1938年4月17日检查了工厂，发现一切正常，但在1938年4月18日发现发电机已被移除。上海经纪行雇用的夜间看守 Fouja Singh 表示，1938年4月17日晚，他在厂内或附近既未听到也未看到任何人；然而，这是可以预料的，因为这名看守白天也在扬州路260号担任 S.P.W.454 职务，因此可以稳妥地推测，他在厂里值班时整夜睡觉，对此他予以否认。

（印：1938年4月25日 特别分部）

On the 22/4/38 permission was obtained from the Dah Kong
Mill to inspect the scene of crime, and together with Mr.S.Hugi-
maru and J.D.S.149 the undersigned on arriving at the scene
found that the stolen dynamos had been removed by some person(s)
who apparently had some experience with such motors as each had
been cleanly removed from its bed and disconnected from its fuse
box without any apparent damage to either. From examination of
dynamos still in the dept. and from markings on the fuse boxes
it was learned that the stolen dynamos bear the following mark-
ings:- "A.E.G." "8h.p." made for the "United China Syndicate".
The number of each dynamo commences with "3926, after which
follows three other numbers thus making a seven figure number.
Efforts were made to trace the complete numbers of the stolen
dynamos by checking the numbers of the dynamos still on the
premises but this proved infructuous as it was found that pre-
ceding numbers of other dynamos were in various depts.

Mr.S.Hugimaru on this occasion was questioned as to what
connection the Dah Kong Mill had with the Heng Foong Mill and
its Italian owners. In reply Mr.S.Hugimaru stated that the Dah
Kong Mill had been placed in control of the Heng Foong Mill by
authority of the Japanese Special Naval Service Mission, Astor
House, and that notices had been placed on all doors of the Heng
Foong Mill prohibiting entry of all persons without permission
of either the Dah Kong Mill or the J.S.N.S.M. Continuing Mr.S
Hugimaru stated that the J.S.N.S.M. were at present negotiating

1938年4月22日，获准进入大康纱厂勘察犯罪现场，笔者与 S. Hugimaru 先生及 J.D.S.149 一同抵达现场后发现，被盗的发电机已被某（些）人搬走，此人显然具备操作此类电机的经验，因为每台发电机均从其基座上被干净利落地拆卸下来，并从保险丝盒断开连接，两者均未受到任何明显损坏。通过检查部门内剩余的发电机以及保险丝盒上的标记，获悉被盗发电机带有以下标记：“A.E.G.”、“8h.p.”，系为“United China Syndicate”制造。每台发电机的编号均以“3926”开头，后跟三个其他数字，从而组成一个七位数编号。曾试图通过核对现场剩余发电机的编号来追踪被盗发电机的完整编号，但此举证明无效，因为发现其他发电机的先前编号分布在各个不同部门。

此次询问了 S. Hugimaru 先生，了解大康纱厂与恒丰纱厂及其意大利业主之间有何关联。S. Hugimaru 先生回答说，根据日本海军特别任务班（Japanese Special Naval Service Mission，位于汇中饭店）的授权，大康纱厂已接管恒丰纱厂的控制权，并且恒丰纱厂的所有门上均已张贴告示，禁止未经大康纱厂或日本海军特别任务班许可的任何人员进入。S. Hugimaru 先生继续表示，日本海军特别任务班目前正在与恒丰纱厂的前业主或其他中方人士进行谈判

Subject Removal of Property from Wing On No. 7 Mill 140 Ningkuo Road.
Two attached letters from Messrs. Melchers attached, dated 6/9/38 & 3/10/38 respectively. C.P. File 2900/183 Y'poo File 75/37 Diary 40.
Made by D. S. I. Kennedy Forwarded by [签名]

Sir,

With reference to the two attached letters from Messrs. Melchers 70 Kiukiang Road, the undersigned and J.D.C. 132 made the following enquiries. At 9 a.m. 30/9/38 Thakar Singh Indian watchman employed by the Wing On Cotton Manufacturing Co. telephoned the station and reported that a motor truck licence No. 15348 had entered the mill. F.S. Duffy attended on the station motor cycle and observed this truck leaving the mill loaded with bales of cotton cloth. He followed the vehicle which was driven along the extension of Ningkuo Road O.O.L. to the Civic Centre where it stopped and unloaded. F.S. Duffy then returned to the station to report the matter.

At 10.30 a.m. 4/10/38 the undersigned and D.S. Stevens in response to another telephone message from Thakar Singh, proceeded to the vicinity of the Wing On No. 7 Mill, and observed the same truck licence No. 15348 loaded with bales of cotton cloth, leaving the mill, and was followed to Ningkuo Road extension O.O.L. where the vehicle was seen proceeding in the direction of the Civic Centre. The only other removal of property from this mill which took place since the two letters from Messrs. Melchers were received at this station, was one hand cart loaded with lengths of steam piping. The hand cart was last seen by the Indian watchman, proceeding East on Pingliang Road. He did not inform the station re this removal of property.

The undersigned and J.D.C. 132 proceeded to the Sacred Heart Hospital, 41 Ningkuo Road this a.m. and interviewed Major Nanaka who is the officer in charge of the Wing On Mill which is at present used as a Military Hospital. Major Nanaka

附有两封来自美最时洋行（Messrs. Melchers）的信函，日期分别为1938年9月6日和1938年10月3日。中央捕房档案 2900/183 杨树浦档案 75/37 日志 40。
由副督察肯尼迪（D. S. I. Kennedy）撰写 转呈 [签名]

先生，

关于所附两封来自九江路70号美最时洋行（Messrs. Melchers）的信件，卑职与第132号华籍侦探（J.D.C. 132）进行了如下调查。1938年9月30日上午9时，受雇于永安纺织制造公司的印度看守塔卡尔·辛格（Thakar Singh）致电警局，报告称一辆牌照号为15348的卡车驶入该厂。警员达菲（F.S. Duffy）骑警用摩托车到场，观察到这辆装载着成包棉布的卡车离开工厂。他尾随该车辆，该车沿宁国路延伸段向外滩方向（O.O.L.）行驶至市中心区域停下并卸货。随后，警员达菲返回警局报告此事。

1938年10月4日上午10时30分，卑职与副督察史蒂文斯（D.S. Stevens）响应塔卡尔·辛格的另一通电话消息，前往永安七厂附近，观察到同一辆牌照号为15348的卡车装载着成包棉布离开工厂，并尾随至宁国路延伸段向外滩方向（O.O.L.），目睹该车辆朝市中心方向驶去。自本局收到美最时洋行的两封信函以来，从该厂移除的其他财产仅有一辆手推车，装载着数段蒸汽管道。印度看守最后看到该手推车沿平凉路向东行驶。他未就此次财产移除事宜通知警局。

卑职与第132号华籍侦探（J.D.C. 132）于今晨前往宁国路41号圣心医院，采访了南卡少校（Major Nanaka），他是目前作为军用医院使用的永安工厂的负责人。南卡少校

Subject Theft of notebook from Wing On Co's private Indian watchman, by
Japanese soldiers.

Made by D. S. Stevens Forwarded by [签名]

Sir,
At 4.30 p.m. 28/9/38, private watchman Karim Baksh, employed
by the Wing On Co. 140 Seoul Road, came to the station and
reported that at 2.30 p.m. 28th inst. he had been stopped by two
Japanese soldiers armed with rifles on Hangchow Road near Seoul
Road, who first asked him, in Chinese, where he worked and then
ordered him to turn out the contents of his pockets. The
watchman handed to them a wallet containing about $3.00, and a
small notebook, the money and wallet were returned to him by
the soldiers, who, however, kept the notebook, after which the
watchman was told to go away. J.D.C.132 attended the scene
and laid the facts before the sentries on duty at the entrance
to the Wing On Company, and also to an officer attached to the
Hospital to which the Wing On Co. has been converted. Nothing
of a useful nature could be obtained, the incident not having
been witnessed by any other Japanese soldiers.

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
REPORT OF POLICE INVESTIGATIONS.

The following is the statement of Thakar Singh,
native of Indian taken by me D. S. Stevens
at Y'poo Stn. on the 6/8/38, and interpreted by S. P. C. 360

My name is Thakar Singh, age 28, father's name Chet
Singh, village and Post Office Sur Singh district Lahore.
I am employed by the Wing On Co. at their mill at 140
Seoul Road as private watchman. At 4.30 p.m. 5/8/38
I, with one foreigner also employed by the company, was
sitting at the corner of Kwangchow & Seoul Roads when we
were approached by three Japanese soldiers armed with
rifles, these men started shouting at us and although we
did not understand what they said we stood up. One soldier
then came to me and pushed me violently, after which one
other loaded his rifle and pointed it at me. They spoke
further to us in Japanese but as we did not understand what
they wanted we remained where we were until the soldiers
left, about five minutes later. One of these soldiers was
one of those concerned in the trouble that I had with
Japanese on the 30/8/38.

Signed.
[签名]
26. 8. 38

上海公共租界工部局警务处。
警方调查报告。

以下是我，警佐史蒂文斯，于1938年8月6日在杨树浦巡捕房对印度籍人士塔卡尔·辛格所作的陈述记录，由特别巡捕360号翻译。

我叫塔卡尔·辛格，28岁，父亲名叫切特·辛格（Chet Singh），村庄及邮局位于拉合尔苏尔·辛格区（Sur Singh district Lahore）。
我在首尔路140号永安公司的纱厂担任私人看守。1938年8月5日下午4时30分，我与另一名同样受雇于该公司的外国人坐在广州路与首尔路的拐角处，此时三名持步枪的日本士兵走近我们，这些人开始对我们大喊大叫，虽然我们要不懂他们在说什么，但我们还是站了起来。随后一名士兵走到我面前，猛烈推搡我，接着另一名士兵给步枪上膛并指向我。他们用日语进一步对我们说话，但由于我们不明白他们的意图，我们留在原地，直到约五分钟后士兵们离开。这些士兵中的一人曾卷入我于1938年8月30日与日本人发生的纠纷中。（注：原文日期此处为30/8/38，与前文8月5日事件及8月6日笔录时间存在逻辑矛盾，照实译出）

property from Wing On No.1 Mill 140 Seoul Road.
Made by D. S. I. Kennedy Forwarded by [Signature]

Sir,
At 3 p.m. 22/8/38 Dr. Korff and Mr. Brewer of Messrs.
Melchers 210 Kiukiang Road came to Yangtszepoo Station as they
wished to examine their property consisting mostly of machinery
removed from the Wing On No.1 Mill 140 Seoul Road, and stored
in Wong On Godown 1616 Y'poo Road. J.D.S. 83 Osano had earlier
in the day had interviewed Major Nanaka who is in charge of the
mill at present. This officer stated that he had already given
the Police permission to visit the godown but would not allow
the representatives of Messrs. Melchers to proceed there.
Major Nanaka was asked to give his reasons for not allowing the
representatives of Messrs. Melchers to inspect their own
property, and gave as explanation that since the commencement
of hostilities, this was the fourth different nationality laying
claims to ownership of the property. The undersigned and
J.D.S.83 accordingly accompanied Dr. Korff to the J.N.L.P.
Special Service Section Hannen Road in order to ascertain whether
it was possible for Messrs. Melchers to remove their property
from the Wing On godown to their own godown on Broadway and also
to check up to ascertain that all the machinery etc. was intact.
Commander Ogawa of the J.N.L.P. on being interviewed advised
Dr. Korff to interview Mr. Tsutsumi of the Japan Cotton Mill
Owners Association in China Yokahama Specie Bank Building, as he
(Mr. Tsutsumi) was in possession of a list of all the property
removed from the Wing On Mill by the staff of the Japan China
Mill 98 Robison Road. Commander Ogawa further intimated that
Dr. Korff make representations regarding the matter to the
German Consul General who in turn would inform the Japanese
Consul General. In the event of the latter issuing the
necessary authorization for the handing over of the machinery

先生，
1938年8月22日下午3时，九江路210号美最时洋行的科夫博士（Dr. Korff）和布鲁尔先生（Mr. Brewer）来到杨树浦巡捕房，因为他们希望查验其财产，这些财产主要是从首尔路140号永安第一纱厂运出并存放在杨树浦路1616号宏安仓库（Wong On Godown）的机器。日本海军陆战队特别服务科83号小野（Osano）少尉当天早些时候曾会见目前负责该纱厂的中田（Nanaka）少校。该军官表示，他已允许警方进入仓库，但不允许美最时洋行的代表前往。
中田少校被问及不允许美最时洋行代表检查其自有财产的原因，他解释说，自敌对行动开始以来，已有四个不同国籍的人声称拥有该财产的所有权。因此，署名人与日本海军陆战队特别服务科83号小野陪同科夫博士前往汉密顿路（Hannen Road）的日本海军陆战队特别服务科，以确定美最时洋行是否有可能将其财产从永安仓库运至其在百老汇路（Broadway）的自有仓库，并核实所有机器等物品是否完好无损。
接受问询的日本海军陆战队小川（Ogawa）指挥官建议科夫博士去横滨正金银行大楼拜访在华日本棉纺业同业公会的堤（Tsutsumi）先生，因为堤先生掌握着由罗宾逊路98号日华纱厂工作人员从永安纱厂运走的所有财产清单。小川指挥官进一步暗示，科夫博士应就此事项向德国总领事提出交涉，由德国总领事转而通知日本总领事。如果后者签发移交机器的必要授权书

Made by D. S. Nicoll Forwarded by C. Thime Asst.

At 4.40p.m. 20/8/38 Thaker Singh p/watchman
employed by the Wing On Co., came to this station and reported that
between 8.25a.m. 19/8/38 and 3.15pm. same date, ten truck-loads of
machinery, one truck-load of cotton-yarn and one truck-load of scales
were removed from the Co's Godown on Seoul Rd. Of the ten loads of
machinery eight proceeded to the Godown at 1616 Yangtszepoo Rd.,
while two went to an unknown destination by way of Lay Rd., the
trucks proceeding north. He further reported that between 8.12a.m.
20/8/38 twelve truck-loads of machinery were also taken from the
same place and transferred to the Godown at 1616 Yangtszepoo Rd
while one truck-load of cotton-cloth and one truck-load of cotton-
yarn were removed to an unknown destination the trucks as before
proceeding by way of Lay Rd., in a northerly direction.
The NO's of the m/trucks are identical with
those given in a previous report, i.e. 17045 and 17054 and were
manned by Chinese coolies with a Japanese civilian in charge.
The truck which removed the cotton-yarn on 20/8/38 was a military
type truck and bore the NO. 5870.
In addition to the above reports Thaker
Singh also reported that on 20/8/38 he and the other p/watchman
one Karimbauks had been approached by two members of the Japanese
Military and a Japanese civilian who stated that they were aware
that the watchmen had been reporting the removal of the property
by the Japanese, to the Police. These three men then searched the
two watchmen and furthermore pushed and jostled them and finally,
before leaving, uttered some threats regarding possible action
should the watchmen continue to report the removal of property to

具报人：D. S. Nicoll 转呈人：助理 C. Thime

1938年8月20日下午4时40分，受雇于永安公司的印籍私人巡更塔克·辛格（Thaker Singh）来到本巡捕房报告称，在1938年8月19日上午8时25分至同日下午3时15分之间，有十卡车机器、一卡车棉纱和一卡车磅秤从该公司位于首尔路（Seoul Rd.）的仓库被运走。在这十车机器中，八车运往杨树浦路1616号的仓库，另外两车经由雷路（Lay Rd.）向北驶往不明目的地。他还报告称，在1938年8月20日上午8时12分，另有十二卡车机器也从同一地点被运走并转移至杨树浦路1616号的仓库，同时有一卡车棉布和一卡车棉纱被运往不明目的地，卡车如前所述经雷路向北行驶。
这些卡车的车牌号与之前报告中提供的相同，即17045和17054，车上由一名日本平民指挥的中国苦力驾驶。
1938年8月20日运走棉纱的卡车是一辆军用卡车，车牌号为5870。
除上述报告外，塔克·辛格还报告称，1938年8月20日，他和另一名巡更卡林博克斯（Karimbauks）被两名日军军人和一名日本平民接近，这些人表示他们知道巡更们一直在向警方报告日本人运走财产的情况。这三个人随后搜查了两名巡更，并对他们推搡拥挤，最后在离开前发出威胁，称如果巡更们继续向警方报告财产被运走的情况，可能会采取行动。

Sir,
On receipt of the above mentioned letter, further enquiries
were made this A.M. by the undersigned and J.D.S. 83 Osano who
proceeded to the Wing On Godown 1616 Yangtszepoo Road. When the
reason for the visit made by the above mentioned detectives was
explained, the warrant officer in charge at the entrance to the
godown on Yangtszepoo Road raised no objection to the undersigned
proceeding to the godown in order to inspect the property
consisting mostly of machinery which had been removed from the
Wing On No.1 Mill, during the past two months. The godown is
composed of two buildings the ground floor of one being practica-
lly packed with spindles and other mill machinery. A Japanese
civilian named T. Hokono employed by the Japan China Cotton Mill
98 Robison Road, when interviewed at the godown, stated that he
was in charge of the machinery and was assisted by a number of
coolies who were engaged in packing and tagging part of it.
Hokono on being questioned stated that the management of the
Japan China Mill 98 Robison Road had been instructed by the
Japanese Military to remove the machinery from the Wing On No.1
Mill to the godown as the former premises were being converted
into a Military hospital.
The undersigned proceeded to Messrs. Melcher's this P.M.
and explained the situation to Dr. Korff. He stated that the
Wing On No.1 Mill was bought in December 1937 by Messrs.
Melcher's but at the time of the sale, all the cotton had been
taken away and practically the only property left on the
premises was the machinery and fittings. Dr. Korff further
stated that representation has already been made to the
Japanese Consulate by the German Consulate regarding the removal
of the machinery, but that he would like to send one of his

具报人：D. S. I. Kennedy 转呈人：[签名] [签名]

先生，
收到上述信件后，具报人与警探 J.D.S. 83 Osano 于今日上午进行了进一步调查，并前往位于杨树浦路1616号的永安仓库。当上述警探说明来访原因后，负责杨树浦路仓库入口的准尉对具报人进入仓库检查财产未提出异议，这些财产主要是过去两个月内从永安第一纱厂移出的机器。该仓库由两座建筑组成，其中一座的底楼几乎堆满了纱锭和其他纺织厂机器。在仓库接受询问时，一名受雇于罗宾森路98号日华纱厂的日本平民 T. Hokono 表示，他负责管理这些机器，并由多名苦力协助包装和标记部分机器。
Hokono 在接受询问时表示，罗宾森路98号日华纱厂的管理层接到日军指令，要求将机器从永安第一纱厂移至该仓库，因为原址正在改建为军医院。
具报人于今日下午前往美最时洋行，并向 Korff 博士说明了情况。他表示，永安第一纱厂已于1937年12月被美最时洋行购买，但在出售时，所有棉花已被运走，实际上留在厂内的财产只有机器和设备。Korff 博士还表示，德国领事馆已就机器被移除一事向日本领事馆提出交涉，但他希望派遣一名员工

Sir,

With reference to the attached letter from Messrs. Melcher
& Co., 10 Kiukiang Road, enquiries were conducted this a.m.
by the undersigned and J. D. S. 83 Osano. The Wing On Godown at
1616 Yangtszepoo Road was visited but owing to the premises
being used at present as barracks for the accomodation of
Japanese troops, entry was not allowed. The Japanese occupants
(civilians) of two trucks parked outside the godown entry on
Yangtszepoo Road were questioned, and they readily admitted
being employees of the China Japan Cotton Mill, 98 Robison Road
and that the Management of this mill had received instructions
from the Japanese Military to remove machinery etc from the Wing
On No. 1 Mill, 140 Seoul Road to the Wing On Godown at 1616
Yangtszepoo Road, as the Wing On No. 1 Mill was being converted
into a Military hospital. (Please see attached report forwarded
by the undersigned on 14/8/38). On being further questioned
regarding whether machinery removed from the Wing On Mill, had
been transported by river from the Wing On godown to the China
Japan Cotton Mill, 98 Robison Road, the informants stated that
the property was not being removed but simply placed in the
godown for safe-keeping.

The undersigned and J. D. S. 83 Osano then proceeded to the
Wing On No. 1 Mill, 140 Seoul Road, (this mill is actually being
converted into a Military Hospital) and interviewed Major Nanaka
who is at present in charge of the building. Major Nanaka
expressed surprise at Messrs. Melcher's claim to ownership of the
machinery in this mill, but repeated that the property was being
removed to the godown for the aforementioned reasons, and there
was no question of said property being disposed of elsewhere.

At 5.30 p.m. August 10, 1938, Thaker Singh, Private
Watchman at the Wing On Cotton Mill, 140 Seoul Road, reported
at Yangtszepoo Station that between 9.50 a.m. and 3.40 p.m.
August 9, 1938, two motor trucks (hire) licence Nos. 17054
and 20322, each manned by two Japanese civilians and ten
Chinese coolies had removed machinery and bales of cotton from
the above mentioned address to an unknown destination. Four
trips were made by the two trucks concerned.

On August 10 Thaker Singh reported that two private
motor trucks licence Nos. 15348 and 20182 each manned by two
Japanese civilians and eight Chinese coolies removed property
of the same description from the mill.

On August 11, the Indian watchman reported that two hire
trucks licence Nos. 17054 and 17045 first manned by ten Chinese
coolies and one Japanese civilian, second manned by ten Chinese
coolies and two Japanese civilians, also removed machinery and
bales of cotton from this mill.

Enquiries were made and it was ascertained that the
property was taken away on instructions issued by the Japanese
Military who gave as explanation that they intended converting
the Wing On Mill, 140 Seoul Road, into a temporary Military
hospital and the machinery and cotton was being transported
to the Wing On Godown at 1616 Yangtszepoo Road for safe keeping.

August 11,1938.

Municipal Council,
Police Force,
Shanghai.

Attention Commissioner Major K.M.Bourne

Dear Sir,

We wish to bring the following to your notice:

Our firm at the end of last year acquired the ownership
of the Wing On Cotton Mill No.1 situated at Lay Road,
Yangtzepoo, and Dah Wah Printing & Dyeing Works including
all machinery, engines and accessories.

The transfer of ownership has been duly registered
with the German Consulate-General which in turn has notified
the Japanese Authorities.

Since the outbreak of hostilities the mill has been
occupied by Japanese Military Forces which have used parts
of the buildings as Military Hospital.

Since the end of July and particularly so during the
last few days we have received reliable reports that
machinery and engine parts and accessories have been
removed without our consent from the mill in trucks.
Details regarding time of removal and licence number of
trucks can be put at your disposal if so required.

We have lodged a serious protest with the German
Consulate-General and we would herewith request you to give
us every assistance in your power to investigate to what
places the truckloads have been removed to and to prevent
further illegal removals of our property.

Requesting you to treat above information as strictly
confidential we would feel obliged if you would inform us
with which department or staff officer we can communicate in
order to discuss the matter further.

Thanking you in anticipation we are,
Dear sir,
Yours faithfully,

尊敬的先生：

我们要提请注意以下事项：

本公司于去年年底收购了位于杨树浦路（Lay Road, Yangtzepoo）的永安第一棉纺厂（Wing On Cotton Mill No.1）以及大华印染厂（Dah Wah Printing & Dyeing Works）的所有权，包括所有机器、引擎及配件。

所有权转让已在德国总领事馆正式登记，该馆已随即通知日本当局。

自战事爆发以来，该厂已被日军占领，部分建筑被用作军用医院。

自7月底以来，特别是最近几天，我们收到可靠报告称，有人未经我方同意，用卡车从工厂运走机器、引擎部件及配件。如有需要，我们可以提供关于搬运时间和卡车牌照号码的详细信息。

我们已向德国总领事馆提出严重抗议，并在此请求贵方尽力协助调查这些卡车将货物运往何处，并防止我们的财产被进一步非法搬移。

鉴于上述信息需严格保密，如蒙告知我们可以与哪个部门或哪位参谋军官联系以进一步讨论此事，我们将不胜感激。

预先致谢，
尊敬的先生，
您忠实的，

offer as well as your shareholders, in which case I
will have no other choice but to report my findings
and disclose your actual connections accordingly.
Please consider all the above very carefully
you as well as all the shareholders and let me know
not later than October 2nd., 1939.
Yours truly,
Yokoyama Boeki Kohshi"
By reading between the lines, this letter
seems to signify that S.Yokoyama is almost at the
end of his tether and is now making his last bid
for the factory; this is more or less confirmed by
the fact that several of the Japanese Companies
to whom Yokoyama has more or less promised the factory
are now about to take action against him in the Japanese
Courts.
Mr. Wilson has been informed that the Police are
unable to render much assistance and was therefore
advised to report to the Japanese Consulate.

I became a coolie at 377 Rangoon Road on 22/8/'38, having
heard from my relative that the factory was going to open under
Japanese control. I was residing at a refugee camp on Kiaochow
Road and was formerly a coolie at the factory before the hostili-
ties. I know that the Japanese are not the owners of the factory.
When I was working in the factory I discovered that the former
employees' belongings were intact and I was approached by one
named Loh Ah Hung to get his 2 daughters' property out of the
factory. The doors of the workers quarters were broken open during
the nights by the coolies employed and sleeping on the premises.
Before day light the doors were nailed up and the property taken
from the rooms was taken away by the coolies who wrapped same
into parcels and took it out of the factory as the 4th. and 5th.
accused were acting as watchmen in the absence of the Japanese.
The 2 Russian watchmen were not allowed to perform their
duty and were instructed that they could live in a room of the
Chinese quarters but could not patrol the factory compound. This
gave the coolies employed ample opportunity to steal during the
night and remove the property during the morning and in the absen-
ce of the Japanese.

On the night of 26/8/38 I had arranged that I would sleep
outside the factory and in the early hours of the morning I
would accompany the 1st. & 2nd. accused also Tsang Miau Fah and Loh
Ah Hung to the back of the factory where by means of a ladder
placed against the wall it was possible to reach a window of one
of the former employees'rooms . Tsang Miau Foh climbed the ladder
and broke the window entered the room and passed the boxes out down to

Remarks
(Any outstanding or peculiar feature to be
commented on by investigating officer).

Prior to the present Sino-Japanese hostilities
the Factory situated at 377 Rangoon Road was known
as the Pioneer Knitting Factory and was managed &
operated by Chinese owners. A portion of the fac-
tory with special machinery was used by the company
to execute a contract given them by a British con-
cern known as the Hien sha Thread Company. Owing
to the hostilities the factory was closed down but
in January 1938 the Hien sha Thread Company com-
menced work at their factory on Yangtsepoo Road
and as they could not get their work completed
without the plant at 377 Rangoon Road being put into
operation it was necessary to lease the factory at
377 Rangoon Road as the company could not get access
to the factory.

The lease of the Pioneer Knitting plant was tak-
en over and the necessary documents filed at the
British Consulate.

In April 1938 the manager of the Pioneer Knit-
ting Factory was approached by a Japanese who attem-
pted to get the company to give him free rights to
operate the factory on their behalf. The manager cal-
led a meeting of directors and shareholders and the
Japanese offer was rejected. The Japanese then took
a threatening attitude and demanded the manager to

在目前的中日敌对行动之前，位于仰光路377号的工厂被称为先锋针织厂，由中国业主管理和经营。工厂的一部分配有专用机器，用于执行一家名为 Hien sha Thread Company 的英国公司给予的合同。由于敌对行动，工厂关闭，但在1938年1月，Hien sha Thread Company 在其杨树浦路工厂开始工作，由于无法在不启用仰光路377号设备的情况下完成工作，因此有必要租赁仰光路377号的工厂，因为该公司无法进入该工厂。

先锋针织厂的租赁权被接管，必要文件已在英国领事馆备案。

1938年4月，一名日本人接触了先锋针织厂经理，试图让公司给予他代表公司运营工厂的自由权利。经理召集了董事和股东会议，拒绝了日本人的提议。随后日本人采取威胁态度，要求经理将工厂经营权移交给她，否则他将由日本军方没收财产。先锋针织厂的业主未理会这些威胁，并收到了几封由日本人写的具有威胁性质的信件。

" 25-8-38. Japanese Consulate have admitted error and

" 29-8-38. Japanese Consulate gave definite instructions

evacuated by Saturday morning. Chinese associated with

" 30-8-38. Japanese still in bleaching & dyeing works.

letting knitting section to Japanese manufacturers im-
plicated in the seizure). We have refused any discussion
until the premises are vacated and passes for Finishing
Dept unobstructed."

case was outlined and remanded for a week.
From information obtained, it would appear that Mr. S. Yokoya-
ma is now trying to obtain the services of the Japanese Special
Military Service Mission to take over the premises on his behalf
and that a great deal of attention is being given to this fact as
the J.N.L.Party and Japanese Consulate are also against any such
action and the 2 parties are now blaming each other for allowing
Mr. S. Yokoyama to go so far but nothing has actually been done to
eject him.
Information also obtained proves that Mr. Kobayashi is threat-
ening to take action against Mr. S. Yokoyama for fraud and Mr. S.
Yokoyama has made an appeal for assistance from the Japanese
Special Military Service Mission.

警长戴维斯（Davies）和巡官克劳奇（Crouch）立即前往，由 J.P.S. 68 号随行，随后督察赫顿（Hutton）也赶到。到达工厂大门时，发现日本人已爬过大门和梯子。
发现多名日本平民，其中确认有 S. 横山先生。在工厂区域内还观察到多名身着制服的日本人，后经证实他们是位于爱麦虞俄路（Maxwell Road）的日本陆军特务机关成员。

他们拒绝打开外门，并让警察去找日本领事馆。

Sir,
At 2.30 p.m. 23-6-38 a telephone message was received from
R.P.C. 60 employed at the former Pioneer Knitting Factory 377
Rangoon Road and now leased to the Mien Hwa Thread Company (British),
reporting that a Japanese was attempting to enter the Factory.

Yokoyama of the Yokoyama Trading Company 20 Canton Road attempt-

he produced a letter of authority to the Japanese Consulate to
take over and operate the Pioneer Knitting Factory. As the owners
of the factory will not negotiate with Mr. S. Yokoyama, he was
informed that the factory had been leased to the Mien Hwa Thread
Company, a British concern, and therefore he could not take over
the premises without instructions from the British Consulate.
Mr. Yokoyama had prior to the arrival of the Police nailed up a
wooden notice on the wall with his name in Japanese. A British
member of the Mien Hwa Thread Company arrived on the scene and
removed the notice which he stated he would take to the British
Consulate.
Mr. Ogden Supt Consul was communicated with and informed of
the visit and action taken.
On 20/15-6-38 Mr. Sia manager of the Pioneer Knitting Factory
received a letter from Messrs. Itoh & Company Osaka regarding

Dear Sir,

With regard to the joint-management of your mill suggested
in my previous letters, I regret very much that my proposal has
failed to receive a favourable response up to the moment.

If I am to take the liberty of expounding my idea for
your consideration once more, you will I write
un-□ □ □ □ □ □ □ □ □ □ □ □ □ □ □ □ □ □ but
regret it means a considerable loss to both you and your
investors to let your excellent plant remain closed indefini-
tely.

A hard obstacle in the way of re-starting the operation is,
I think, the fact that the plant is situated in the special area
because of which a permit from the Japanese authorities is nece-
ssary for the re-opening of the mill.

Recently I have happened to hear that the operation of your
bleaching factory has been committed to a certain English, and
you have sought an understanding in this respect with the Japan-
ese authorities through the British Consulate. I am afraid,
however, that such an arrangement as above might prove success-
ful in no way but rather result in irritating the Japanese au-
thorities in your territory.

As to the operation of the mill I am fully convinced that
there could be no better way than to run the mill in conjunction
with the Japanese entrepreneurs, and in this way the authorities'
permit is to be obtained quickly.

With the view to facilitate the project I have had several
talks with the staff of the Naigai Amimono Kabushiki Kaisha (The
Naigai Hosiery Mill. Ltd) about the desirability of running your
mill by yourself, the Naigai Hosiery Mill, Ltd and C. Itoh & Co.,
Ltd. co-jointly.

关于我在前几封信中建议的贵厂合资经营事宜，非常遗憾，我的提议至今未获积极回应。

若容许我再次阐述我的想法以供阁下考虑，我将写道
un-□ □ □ □ □ □ □ □ □ □ □ □ □ □ □ □ □ □ 但
遗憾的是，让贵方优良的厂房无限期闲置，意味着阁下及
您的投资者都将遭受重大损失。

我认为，重新开工的一个主要障碍是，该厂房位于

可。

As you are well aware of, our firm has been in the closest
connection with the Nippon Hosiery Mill, Ltd. which is one of
the leading hosiery manufacturers in this country, being espe-
cially known for their skill in the mens socks manufacture.
Fortunately enough, the Nippon Hosiery Mill, Ltd. is very much
inclined to participate in the management of your mill, and Mr.
Kiichi Toh, Managing Director of the said Mill, is coming over
to your city for having personal talks with you about the de-
tails of the joint-management in question.

I do wish you will give your best consideration to the matter
so that the proposed joint-management by these two firms will
be realized as quickly as possible.

I am also convinced that this measure is very significant in
that, by carrying out this plan, we are able to discharge our
share in the promotion of economic friendship between your coun-
try and ours which is so badly needed in all quarters at
present.

Of course, I could well surmise certain circumstances on
your side which might have made the immediate realisation of my
proposal difficult, but I earnestly wish that you would recon-
sider the project from a broader point of view and do your best
possible efforts for the re-starting of your mill in the inter-
ests of both yourself and your investors.

Awaiting your favourable reply at an early date,

Sir,

On 11-6-38 Mr. Sia, manager and shareholder of the Pioneer
Knitting Factory, informed that he had received a letter from
Mr. S. Yokoyama in which he again stated he had been appointed
by the Japanese Consulate General and Military Headquarters to
take over the operating of the Pioneer Knitting Factory. Copy
of letter reads as follows:-

S. Yekeyama,
20 Derrech Road,
June 10, 1938.

T.W. Sha Esq.,
Present.

Dear Mr. Sha,

On April 12th, I spoke to you regarding the management
of your first mill for the purpose of protecting your interest,
I had expected to receive your answer by April 16th, but you
failed to answer me, on the 21st of April you stated that you
had made arrangement with Mr. Kuniki of Itoh & Co., and I re-
member you stated that in case you fail to fix up through Itoh
& Co., you would get in touch with me for arranging the matter.

I must inform you that the Japanese Consulate-General and
Military Headquarters have refused to even consider permitting
Mr. Kuniki to operate your matter. But I am appointed officially
by the two above mentioned authorities to manage and operate
your mill.

I understand that you have asked a certain British Firm
"Min Wha Thread Co. through the British Consulate-General to
operate your mill, but this has also been refused by the Japan-
ese Government, of which I am certain you have been advised.

As will be seen from the first report regarding the
Pioneer Knitting Factory, Mr. Sia was being continually annoyed
by Japanese, approaching him for the taking over of his factory.
For many years prior to the present hostilities, the Pioneer
Knitting Factory operated a dyeing plant at the same address and
all the work of the Mien Wha Thread Company Ltd (Messrs. Coates,
Paisley) (British) was done on the premises. This resulted in
godowns and goods belonging to the Mien Wha Company being stored
in the building. The Mien Wha Company have been extremely busy
and as they had not the necessary plant to dye the amount of
goods ordered they approached Mr. Sia and requested to take his
premises over on a lease. Mr. Sia readily agreed to lease the
premises to the British Company and Mr. Edmonds, manager of the
Mien Wha Company, immediately interviewed Mr. Ogden at H.B.M.
Consulate where a letter was sent to the Japanese Consulate
informing them that the British Company were taking over the
Pioneer Knitting Factory and expressed the hope that the Japanese
Consulate would co-operate and give all the assistance possible.

Passes were then obtained by Mr. Edmonds for workers to
enter the district and put the machinery in working order and up
to the present time no interference has taken place.

Mr. Sia stated that he would refuse to interview Mr. S.
yama and Mr. Edmonds interviewed Mr. Ogden and gave him a

Subject Yokoyama Trading Company, 20 Canton Road.
Made by D.S.I. Kao Yen-ken Forwarded by C. Casada. A.D.

The Yokoyama Trading Company is solely a Japanese transportation firm with an office at Room 311, 20 Canton Road. The principal business of this company is the removal of goods on behalf of applicants with property north of the Soochow Creek now under the control of the Japanese military and naval authorities. A number of Japanese in military uniform frequent the office daily.

With reference to the attempt by a Japanese subject named S. Yokoyama to force the Pioneer Knitting Factory, a Chinese concern on Rangoon Road, to transfer its interests, information received is to the effect, that the Kong Tai Hosiery Factory, 1082 Ward Road (a Japanese firm), was really the interests behind the suggested selling of the Pioneer Knitting Factory. The Kong Tai Hosiery Factory management, it is learned, requested Mr. K. Ohyama of Itoh & Co., 110 Hankow Road, to approach Mr. Sia Wei-nan (謝渭南), the Manager of the Pioneer Factory, because of his friendship with Mr. Sia, for the transfer of the interests, but the request was not entertained. Being met with a refusal from this quarter, the Kong Tai Factory then entrusted the matter to the Yokoyama Trading Company, with the resultant visit by Mr. Yokoyama.

Although discreet enquiries have been carried out, no information has been obtained of a foreigner being connected in any way with the Yokoyama Trading Company.

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE - 4 MAY 1938 SPECIAL BRANCH）

Kao Yen-ken

横山洋行仅是一家日本运输公司，办公地点位于广东路20号311室。该公司的主要业务是代表申请人搬运货物，这些申请人的财产位于苏州河以北，目前处于日本海陆军当局控制之下。多名身着军装的日本人每日频繁出入该办公室。

关于一名名为 S. Yokoyama 的日本籍人士试图强迫位于仰光路的华商企业先锋针织厂（Pioneer Knitting Factory）转让其权益一事，所获情报显示，华德路1082号的公泰袜厂（Kong Tai Hosiery Factory，一家日商企业）实际上是幕后推动出售先锋针织厂利益的势力。据悉，公泰袜厂管理层因与谢渭南先生（Mr. Sia Wei-nan，先锋厂经理）有交情，曾请求汉口路110号伊藤洋行（Itoh & Co.）的 K. Ohyama 先生接洽谢先生以转让权益，但该请求未获受理。在此处碰壁后，公泰厂遂将此事委托给横山洋行，从而导致了横山先生的到访。

尽管已进行谨慎查访，但未获得任何外国人与横山洋行有任何关联的情报。

日本军方对先锋针织厂的财产恐怕不会手软。

谢先生的侄子告知 Yokoyama 先生，由于工厂并非谢先生一人所有，在做出任何决定前必须召开股东会议。Yokoyama 先生随即变得更具攻击性，并表示如果该侄子不相信他代表日本军方，可以打电话至广东路20号核实。

然而，谢先生的侄子坚持认为，在不咨询公司股东的情况下无法采取任何行动。因此，Yokoyama 先生给予其时间考虑答复并召开股东会议，截止日期为1938年4月15日。当时指出，股东并非全在上海，不可能在15日前给出答复；于是日期延至1938年4月底，届时必须出具一封承诺与日本人合作的信函，否则将采取严厉行动。身穿便服的 Yokoyama 先生随后走出办公室。第二名男子在警告谢先生的侄子最好服从指令，否则公司利益将受损后，于几分钟后离开。

在获取上述信息后，谢先生似乎因受到威胁而感到不安，被告知识若访客再次前来，应找借口留住他们并与中央捕房联系，因为这两人可能企图勒索钱财或以分成方式获取公司权益。

先锋针织厂是目前战事中少数未被日本人破坏的场所之一。虽有多起 petty larcenies（轻微盗窃）报案，但并无

Mr. P.Y. Bunyun Yu(虞炳榮), Compradore of the
S.A. Racine & Cie, 2 Peking Road, has voluntarily offered
the following information.
Mr. Yu is a shareholder of the Hua Tung Tobacco
Factory, 902 Tongshan Road, near Paoting Road. The factory
closed in August, 1937, as a result of the Sino-Japanese
hostilities. The machinery, materials and buildings are
intact and are worth about a million dollars. The manager
and principal shareholder Lea Yau Tung(黎耀東) is a
Cantonese living in Rue Bourgeat. He has received an offer
from a certain Japanese syndicate through the medium of the
Japanese Military for the purchase of the property for
$300,000. Lea ignored the offer but the Japanese authorities
have served a summons on him to make a call in Hongkew without
fail otherwise the property would be confiscated or removed.
Lea became so worried that he fell sick and has entered
a hospital. Mr. Yu and some other friends are advising him
to leave for Hongkong
Information from other sources is to the effect that
the factory has been taken over by Japanese and is now in
operation.

FILE

2/7.

D. C. (Special Branch)

北京路2号赛生洋行（S.A. Racine & Cie）买办虞炳荣先生（Mr. P.Y. Bunyun Yu）自愿提供以下信息。

虞先生是同山路902号、近保定路的华东烟草厂的股东。该厂因中日战事于1937年8月关闭。机器、材料和建筑物完好无损，价值约一百万美元。经理兼主要股东黎耀东先生（Lea Yau Tung）是一名居住在蒲石路（Rue Bourgeat）的广东人。他通过日本军方收到某日本财团的报价，欲以30万美元购买该财产。黎先生无视该报价，但日本当局向他发出传票，勒令其务必前往虹口报到，否则财产将被没收或搬走。黎先生因此忧心成疾，已入院治疗。虞先生及其他一些朋友正劝其前往香港。

来自其他来源的信息显示，该厂已被日本人接管，目前正在运营。

Made by D.I. Hutton. Forwarded by [Signature]

Sir,
At 12.30 p.m. 15-4-38 members of the Japanese Naval Landing Party escorted to this station 2 motor trucks loaded with cigarette making machinery. Enquiries were made by D.I. Hutton but the chauffeur a Russian named Terloff could not give a very convincing story of how and where he obtained the machinery.
One of the Russians in charge of the operations being known to the undersigned as being an employee of the Shanghai Brokerage Company with offices at 405 Hongkong Shanghai Bank Building, was interrogated and admitted that he had received instructions to convey the machinery from the Don Bosco School Hanchow Road Yangtsepoo District (Silician Institute) to a vacant piece of ground on Baikal Road.
As the machinery was of value and if left unattended it would undoubtedly be seized by Japanese, the Russian was instructed to leave the machinery in the station whilst enquiries were continued at the Shanghai Brokerage Office. The manager of the company was not present and enquiries were therefore made at the office of Dr. Constantine, Lawyer, Rue Chu Pao San, where it was ascertained that a Mr. Wei, a shareholder of the Ha Tung Tobacco Company and a Roman Catholic by religion had requested Father Fontana in charge of the Silician Institute to remove the machinery from the Ha Tung Cigarette Factory 902 Tongshan Road and if possible to transport same south of the Creek.
The removal was therefore arranged and a Bill of Sale was given by Mr. Wei in favour of the Shanghai Brokerage Company who were instructed to remove the property to the Don Bosco School, pending a favourable opportunity for transportation from the school.
After the removal of machinery a Japanese concern wished to

先生，
1938年4月15日下午12时30分，日本海军陆战队成员护送两辆装载卷烟制造机器的卡车来到本捕房。警探长 Hutton 进行了询问，但司机是一名名叫 Terloff 的俄国人，他对于如何以及从哪里获得这些机器的说法并不令人信服。
负责行动的一名俄国人被下文签署人确认为上海经纪行（Shanghai Brokerage Company）的员工，该行办事处位于香港上海银行大楼405室，经讯问，他承认接到指示将机器从杨树浦区杭州路的鲍思高学校（即司立修学院（Silician Institute））运至贝加尔路（Baikal Road）的一块空地上。
由于机器具有价值，若无人看管无疑会被日本人扣押，因此指示该俄国人在继续向上海经纪行查询期间，将机器留在捕房内。该公司经理不在，因此向朱葆三路（Rue Chu Pao San）律师 Constantine 博士的办公室进行了查询，经查实，华东烟草公司的股东、天主教徒魏先生（Mr. Wei）曾请求负责司立修学院的 Fontana 神父将机器从同山路902号的华东卷烟厂移出，并尽可能将其运至苏州河以南。
因此安排了搬迁，魏先生出具了一份卖契给上海经纪行，指示他们将财产移至鲍思高学校，以待从学校转运的有利时机。
机器搬走后，一家日本商社希望

Sir,
Reference to attached complaint from Mr. S.T. Miyahara,
the following is an extract from the Occurrence Book of
Yulin Road Station, relating to the removal of property from
the Wha Tung Tobacco Company (華東煙草公司) 902 Tongshan Road.
12.30 p.m. The Japanese Naval Landing Party brought to this station
13.4.38. a Russian chauffeur, named Terloff, employed by the "Economic
Transport Company" 150 Kiukiang Road, who was removing machinery
from a piece of waste land on Yangtsepoo Road and placing
same on a piece of waste land on Baikal Road near Whashing Road.
The Japanese Naval Landing Party refused to allow the
Russian chauffeur to proceed with his work ordering him to take
the machinery back to where he had taken it from.
Enquiries from the "Economic Transport Company" ascertained
that they had received an order for a m/truck and four Chinese
coolies to remove same to Baikal Road, owners residing at 902
Tongshan Road.
The Russian chauffeur did not have any papers or proof
that the machinery was the property of any legal owner and
admitted that it was Chinese machinery.
Remarks:
D.S. Rhodes enquiries.
Property brought to station on D.I. Hutton request.
Enquiries proceeding.
This property consisted of 1 cigarette making machine, and
7 machines used in the shredding of tobacco in the process of
manufacturing cigarettes, and from investigations made at the
Wha Tung Tobacco Company together with Mr. Miyahara, had
obviously been removed from these premises.

先生，
关于附上的宫原先生（Mr. S.T. Miyahara）的投诉，以下是榆林路捕房日志中关于从华东烟草公司（華東煙草公司）同山路902号移除财产的摘录。
下午12时30分。1938年4月13日，日本海军陆战队将一名名叫 Terloff 的俄国司机带到本捕房，他受雇于九江路150号的“经济运输公司”（Economic Transport Company），当时他正将机器从杨树浦路的一块荒地移走，并放置在华兴路（Whashing Road）附近的贝加尔路（Baikal Road）的一块荒地上。
日本海军陆战队拒绝让该俄国司机继续工作，命令他将机器搬回原处。
向“经济运输公司”查询后查明，他们收到订单，要求提供一辆机动卡车和四名中国苦力，将物品运至贝加尔路，货主居住在同山路902号。
该俄国司机没有任何文件或证据证明机器属于任何合法所有者，并承认这是中国机器。
备注：
警佐 Rhodes 查询。
应警探长 Hutton 要求将财产带至捕房。
查询正在进行中。
该财产包括1台卷烟机和7台在卷烟制造过程中用于切丝的机器，经过对华东烟草公司及与宫原先生一起进行的调查，这些机器显然是从该处所移出的。

03038
CHINA PRESS.
MAR 21 1939

Nippon Tobacco Men Declared
Running Seized Chinese Plants

Cigarettes Manufactured By Factories Reported
Flooding Shanghai Market; Thousands Of
Workers Said Engaged In Operations

Operating with looted materials
from other Chinese plants, seven
seized Chinese cigarette factories
now under Japanese management,
are pouring their products into
the Shanghai tobacco market, a
Chinese report said yesterday.

All seven factories have been
reorganized by the Japanese, it
was revealed, and are producing
more than ten brands of cigarettes
now circulating in this city.

The Chung Yuan factory at the
corner of Paoting and Kunming
Roads, has been renamed Hwa
Sen No. 1, hiring 800 workers.
Operation of this factory began
more than a year ago.

Resumes 8 Months Ago

Resuming operating eight months
ago, the Sin Hwa factory on Tang-
shan Road, now known as Hwa
Sen No. 2, is employing 300 workers.
A Chinese, named Chow Miao-
kan, was said to be helping the
Japanese in the enterprise.

The Hwa Tung factory on Pao-
ting and Tangshan Roads has
been reorganized into the Tung Ya-
(East Asia) factory. Five hundred
workers have been working in this
plant since six months ago.

Renamed respectively as Kung
Sen No. 1 and No. 2, the Sin Min
factory and the Chung Nan factory
have been operating for several
months with 1,000 workers.

Looted Goods Used

According to the report, the raw
material used in the Hwa Sen
factories was looted from the
Nanyang Brothers Tobacco Factory,
and the Hwa Chen Tobacco Factory
in Hongkew.

Among the brands of cigarettes
produced by the Hwa Sen factories
were said to be the Pei Hua
(Hundred Flowers), Mo Tun
(Modern), and Huang Pian Fu
(Yellow Bat).

The products of the Kung Sen
factories were said to include the
following brands: "Mei To," "Wu
Lum", "Li Pai Tang" (church),
and "Hueng Si Pao".
pages.zh:
03038
《大陆报》。
1939年3月21日

宣称日本人经营被占中国工厂

据报道，这些工厂生产的香烟充斥上海市场；据悉数千工人参与运营

一家中文报纸昨日称，七家被占领的中国卷烟厂目前由日本人管理，利用从其他中国工厂掠夺来的原料进行生产，并将其产品涌入上海烟草市场。

据悉，所有七家工厂均已由日本人重组，目前正生产十多个品牌的香烟，并在本市流通。

位于保定路和昆明路路口的中原烟厂已更名为华生第一厂，雇佣工人800名。该厂的运营始于一年多以前。

八个月前恢复运营

位于唐山路的新华烟厂于八个月前恢复运营，现名为华生第二厂，雇佣工人300名。据悉，一名叫周妙根（Chow Miao-kan，音译）的中国人正在协助日本人经营该企业。

位于保定路和唐山路的华通烟厂已重组为东亚（Tung Ya）烟厂。五百名工人自六个月前起就在该厂工作。

新民烟厂和中南烟厂分别更名为公生第一厂和第二厂，已有1000名工人在此工作了数月。

使用掠夺物资

据报道，华生各厂使用的原料是从南洋兄弟烟草公司和位于虹口的华成烟草厂掠夺而来的。

据说华生各厂生产的香烟品牌包括“百花”（Pei Hua）、“摩登”（Mo Tun）和“黄蝙蝠”（Huang Pian Fu）。

据说公生各厂的产品包括以下品牌：“美多”（Mei To）、“五伦”（Wu Lum）、“礼拜堂”（Li Pai Tang）和“红双炮”（Hueng Si Pao）。

SHANGHAI EVENING POST & MERCURY. JUL 1 9 1938
01731

A Direct Challenge
IT WILL BE INTERESTING to discover what happens in the case of the Shanghai Portland Cement Works at Lunghwa.
This is a well known Chinese enterprise, taken over by the Japanese following the Chinese troops' withdrawal from the Shanghai area and recently said to have been operated by the Onoda Cement Company for production of cement locally marketed.
Now Siemssen and Company, a Shanghai German firm, has made known that it has taken over ownership of the works and has announced that as the properties of the factories have been assigned by deed of transfer, warning is given against encroachment upon the factory premises.
Here we have a direct challenge which may prove a test of the recent Japanese-announced intentions with regard to Chinese industries. Consider:
The Japanese have said that they would take over and operate Chinese industrial properties in the event that the Chinese owners refused their offers of "co-operation". Experience has shown that Chinese owners of large enterprises cannot resume without special permission which quite obviously has entailed concessions by the Chinese, usually including taking Japanese in as "partners". The Japanese have said they would recognize bona fide sales to non-Chinese, even when these occurred after the hostilities, but in practice there has been—as in the recently much-publicised case of the Chun Tah cotton mill—unwillingness to recognize even what seem to others a clear case of this sort. Additionally there is a general contention that the Chinese and non-Japanese foreigners have precisely as much right to "co-operate", on their own terms and without reference to or review by any Japanese authority, as the Chinese and the Japanese.
The foregoing sums up the general facts of the background. In the case of the cement plant sale we have no information as to the terms of the sale, and we tend increasingly to feel that it is a sound view that even the "emergency situation"—there being no formalized state of war in any event—in no way justifies the Japanese or anyone else in arguing that the terms have any bearing on the matter unless the Japanese wish frankly to say that the Open Door in China no longer exists and that, in effect, they are as much at odds with other countries on the economic front as they are with China on the military front.

What is particularly interesting is the fact that the present case involves a German firm. Japan does not want to quarrel with Germany. She has very few friends today, and neither the Germans nor the Italians in China are enthusiastic over a situation which is costing them their whole stake here; but thus far, Japan continues to keep Berlin and Rome more or less on her side. Can this situation persist if in addition to the general causes for complaint already in existence, Japan flatly refuses to recognise German purchase rights under any circumstances which the Germans themselves consider valid?
Thus far, the tug-of-war has involved the British mostly and although Japan has of late warmed up to Britain after a period of bristling near-hostility, still a rather obstinate attitude has been maintained even with reference to purchase cases like the Chun Tah one where there is a mass of convincing evidence of the fullest validity, plus official British recognition of the fact.
Certainly the position must become increasingly puzzling for the Japanese since they cannot court a battle-royal with everyone, including the Germans and the Italians; yet on the other hand if they do not in some measure stick to their guns on announced policy, it is easy to see that there will be a rush by the Chinese to sell out in virtually any quarter rather than submit their properties to compulsory Japanese "operation" which seems only a thinly-veiled confiscation.
All this might have been avoided, of course, if the Japanese had been willing to make their campaign a straightforward military affair leaving economic matters to be dealt with later. But from the outset, the economic side has been to the fore—a thing involving few complications when it centered about such matters, for example, as mining coal and iron in North China, but a thing bound to develop increasing complexities as it extended into the industrial field of Shanghai. We don't envy the Japanese their job of finding the answers in a situation likely to become steadily more thorny as it develops additional international aspects.

01731

直接挑战

龙华上海水泥厂一案的结果如何，这将是一件有趣的事。这是一家知名的中国企业，在中国军队撤离上海地区后被日本人接管，最近据说由小野田水泥公司（Onoda Cement Company）运营，生产在当地市场销售的水泥。
现在，上海德商西门子洋行（Siemssen and Company）已宣布其已取得该厂的所有权，并声明由于工厂财产已通过转让契据分配，警告不得侵犯工厂场地。
这是一个直接的挑战，可能会检验日本最近宣布的关于中国工业的意图。请看：
日本人曾表示，如果中国业主拒绝他们的“合作”提议，他们将接管并运营中国工业财产。经验表明，大型企业的中国业主未经特别许可无法复工，而这显然需要中国方面做出让步，通常包括接纳日本人作为“合伙人”。日本人曾表示承认向非中国人进行的善意出售，即使这些出售发生在战事之后，但在实践中，正如最近广为宣传的申达棉纺厂一案那样，他们甚至不愿承认在别人看来是此类明确案例的情况。此外，还有一种普遍的观点认为，中国人与非日本籍外国人完全有权按照自己的条件进行“合作”，无需参考或接受任何日本当局的审查，这与中国人和日本人之间的合作权利相同。
以上概括了背景的一般事实。关于这家水泥厂的出售，我们没有关于出售条款的信息，我们越来越倾向于认为，即使是“紧急情况”——毕竟无论如何都没有正式的战争状态——也绝不能成为日本人或其他任何人辩称这些条款与此事有关的理由，除非日本人坦率地表示中国的门户开放政策已不复存在，并且实际上，他们在经济战线上与其他国家的矛盾如同在军事战线上与中国的矛盾一样深。
特别有趣的是，本案涉及一家德国公司。日本不想与德国争吵。她今天的朋友很少，在华的德国人和意大利人对这种使他们失去在这里全部利益的局面并不热情；但到目前为止，日本继续让柏林和罗马或多或少站在她这一边。如果除了已经存在的普遍抱怨原因之外，日本在任何德国人自己认为有效的情况下都断然拒绝承认德国的购买权，这种情况还能持续吗？
到目前为止，这场拉锯战主要涉及英国，尽管日本在经过一段剑拔弩张的近敌对时期后近期对英国态度缓和，但即使在像申达一案这样有充分有效性的大量令人信服的证据加上英国官方承认事实的情况下，日本仍保持着相当顽固的态度。
毫无疑问，日本的处境必定变得越来越令人困惑，因为他们不能与所有人，包括德国人和意大利人，进行全面战斗；但另一方面，如果他们在某种程度上不坚持已宣布的政策，很容易看到中国人会急于向 virtually 任何方面出售资产，而不是将其财产提交给强制性的日本“运营”，这似乎只是 thinly-veiled 的没收。
当然，如果日本人愿意使其战役成为单纯的军事事务，将经济问题留待以后处理，这一切本可以避免。但从一开始，经济方面就处于前沿——当它集中在例如在华北开采煤铁等问题上时，这涉及很少的复杂性，但随着它扩展到上海的工业领域，必然会产生日益复杂的局面。我们不羡慕日本人在一个随着发展出更多国际层面而可能变得愈发棘手的局面中寻找答案的工作。
